  "variants": [

      "id": "V1",
      "title": "Conductivity-conditioned generation of disordered Li-halide solid electrolytes",
      "text": "Battery crystal discovery, restricted to the disordered Li-halide solid electrolytes where fast Li conduction actually lives. Crystal foundation models: there's hella, but MatterGen's <=20-atom unit-cell limit and stable ordered-crystal training set do not cover the partially-occupied configurations that fast Li conductors need. Fine-tune MatterGen's adapter on predicted ionic conductivity using DTU's 400k-structure halide database as the domain-specific transport label source, generate and screen 1k-100k candidates per arm, NEB-validate the top ten, and compare hit rate against unconditioned generation and ICSD screening, all within the halide family. Compute axis: generated candidate crystal structures screened per arm, 1,000-100,000 candidates, 3 levels.",
      "root_link": "is the root question",
      "compute_open": "whether halide-domain fine-tuning shifts the hit-rate gap outside seed noise",
      "sequential": "not given (seed idea from notes)",
      "changes": "System studied: generic Li conductors -> disordered, partially-occupied Li-halide solid electrolytes fine-tuned on DTU's 400k-structure halide database. Closes gap 2 (MatterGen's ordered <=20-atom training set vs the structurally disordered halides where fast conduction lives) and aims the result at DTU Energy's MatterGen -> MatterSim -> DFT electrolyte pipeline."
    },
    {
      "id": "V2",
      "title": "Spend the compute on NEB-validated candidates, scored against measured conductivity",
      "text": "Battery crystal discovery, with the compute spent on deeper validation rather than more generation. Fine-tune MatterGen's adapter on predicted log conductivity, generate candidates, then scale the number per arm that receive DFT-NEB migration-barrier validation from the top ten up to the top 100-1,000, comparing against unconditioned generation and ICSD screening. Score candidates by NEB barriers and predicted conductivity calibrated against the measured conductivity of PNNL's synthesized NaxLi3-xYCl6 family rather than predicted sigma alone. Compute axis: NEB-validated candidates per arm, 10-1,000 candidates, 3 levels.",
      "root_link": "is the root question",
      "compute_open": "whether the conditioned generator's ranking survives NEB validation against measured halide conductivity data",
      "sequential": "not given (seed idea from notes)",
      "changes": "Quantity more compute buys: generated-and-screened candidate count -> DFT-NEB-validated candidates per arm, with top candidates scored against PNNL's measured NaxLi3-xYCl6 conductivity. Closes gap 3 (NEB barriers and predicted log-conductivity vs the measured conductivity the programmes need) and aims at the PNNL-Microsoft battery collaboration."
    },
    {
      "id": "V3",
      "title": "Benchmark conditioned generation against Azure Quantum Elements' 32-million-candidate screen",
      "text": "Battery crystal discovery, judged against the front-end Microsoft actually uses. Fine-tune MatterGen's adapter on predicted ionic conductivity, generate and screen 1k-100k candidates per arm, NEB-validate the top ten, and compare hit rate not against ICSD screening but against Azure Quantum Elements' 32-million enumerated-candidate screen. The question becomes whether conductivity-conditioned generation beats enumeration on hit rate per candidate proposed. Compute axis: generated candidate crystal structures screened per arm, 1,000-100,000 candidates, 3 levels.",
      "root_link": "is the root question",
      "compute_open": "whether conditioning beats the 32-million enumeration screen only at the 100,000-candidate level",
      "sequential": "not given (seed idea from notes)",
      "changes": "Comparison judged against: ICSD database screening -> Azure Quantum Elements' 32-million enumerated-candidate screen. Makes the result speak directly to Microsoft Research AI for Science's MatterGen / Azure Quantum Elements battery programme (with PNNL), testing whether conductivity-conditioned generation improves on the enumeration front-end they use today."
    }
  ]
}
